subject: Pilot credits & burn-rate check-in — next steps and extension request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot credits & burn-rate check-in — recap + next steps

Hi Alicia — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

1) Current pilot status:
- You’ve been ingesting EHR excerpts + appointment data into the summarization pipeline.
- Last 7 days: ~420K tokens/day (inbound + generated) per your export.

2) Key ask from Acme:
- Keep the pilot running through mid-May to validate 1) classification accuracy on clinical notes and 2) latency for in-clinic use.
- Need an additional credit top-up if current burn continues.

3) Pricing/qualification notes (from our side):
- Target unit economics discussion: our hosted rate for the model variant you’re using is $1,200 / 1M tokens (list before discounts).
- For pilots we typically target a blended target of $800-$1,000 / 1M after credits and pilot pricing depending on expected steady-state volumes.
- If you plan to scale beyond 1M tokens/day we’ll review Dedicated options (reserved capacity) which can materially reduce $/1M.

4) Proposed next steps:
- I can approve a one-week credit extension of $5,000 to cover the next 7–10 days of burn if that matches your needs.
- Please confirm expected daily token burn over the next 10 days (best estimate) so we can size the extension.
- If you think you’ll hit >1.5M tokens/day, flag that — we’ll pull in Product to discuss batching/quantization recommendations.

Attachments: I’ve attached the usage CSV you shared (acme-usage-report-0427.csv) and a short pilot-extension form (pilot-agreement.pdf) we can sign for the credit.

Thanks — happy to chat through the numbers live if easier.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Thanks, Marissa — very helpful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 420K tokens/day was an average over the last week; yesterday spiked to ~650K because a batch import included full visit transcripts. Going forward we expect 400K–800K/day depending on ingestion cadence.
- Our narrow budget for this pilot is $12k for additional credits before we convert to a paid agreement. If you can approve $5k now, that covers roughly the next 7–10 days at current averages but won’t handle a sustained 800K/day.
- Can you confirm how long it typically takes to process a DocuSign extension? We need internal procurement approval language on scope + data handling.

If helpful, Tom and I can jump on a quick 15-min call this afternoon to finalize the amount and sign the extension.

—Alicia

Subject: Re: Pilot credits & burn-rate check-in — recap + next steps

Thanks for the details, Alicia — that helps. Quick answers and an ask: 

- Approvals & timing: I can sign off on a $5,000 credit extension immediately (I’ve budgetary authority for pilot top-ups). DocuSign turnaround for the form is typically same-day once you confirm — procurement usually needs the simple SOW language we included in pilot-agreement.pdf.
- Unit economics: given the 400K–800K/day estimate, your steady-state monthly run rate could be ~12M–24M tokens. At our list $1,200/1M tokens that’s $14.4k–$28.8k/month. With pilot credits/discounts we typically target the $9.6k–$19.2k/month band (which maps to $800–$1,000 per 1M tokens).
- If you want to cap spend, we can set a daily quota and alert thresholds in the Console. Recommend a hard daily cap at 900K tokens for now to avoid surprise spikes while you finish ingestion clean-up.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) I’ll provision the $5k credit once you confirm that’s what you want (reply OK).
2) If you want DocuSign, reply with the signatory name and I’ll push the DocuSign link to you today.
3) If you want to lock a short-term daily cap (we’ll configure in Console) tell me the cap and an emergency contact.

I’ve attached the pilot agreement for your procurement team to review; highlighted the data handling and retention section for Acme’s compliance folks.

Thanks — I’ll hold on the top-up until I hear back.

Best,
Marissa
